fields.v: Meawad, F. (2026). Design-First Governance for Reliable AI-Assisted Software Development. In 2026 IEEE 23rd International Conference on Software Architecture Companion (ICSA-C), pp. 194-198. IEEE. DOI: 10.1109/ICSA-C68850.2026.00048
Conference — 2026 IEEE 23rd International Conference on Software Architecture Companion (ICSA-C), pp. 194-198; short paper, 5 pages
fields.why: The text does not say which track of the ICSA companion volume this is (workshop, new-ideas or main companion track), so Workshop is possible.

fields.v: Research and Engineering, SOKNA, Egypt (single author; company)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Compares — Design-First Governance (contract-driven toolchain + executable guardrails); initial evaluation of governed vs non-governed prompting with three LLMs in two studies (Setup, Extension)

A: Design-First Governance (author's own), with the author's custom toolchain openapi-forge and openapi-js-generator plus agent skills for both; versions Not stated. B (baseline): non-governed prompting (no skills, tools or guardrails in Setup; tools present but not referenced in Extension)

Prisma schema (schema.prisma) as single source of truth (domain models and relationships); generated OpenAPI 3.1 specification (openapi.json) with manual path/component overrides (specs/); forge.config.js and openapi-gen.config.js; generated TypeScript types and N-tier backend (routes, controllers, services, formatters, repositories, middleware, infrastructure); guardrail configs: Spectral rules, eslint.config.mjs (architectural rules), .dependency-cruiser.js (layer boundaries); API contract tests; agent skills for the two generators

Setup phase: developer defines Prisma schema -> openapi-forge generates OpenAPI 3.1 spec (validated with Spectral) -> openapi-js-generator scaffolds a functional N-tier app. Extension phase: specification update (Prisma schema or OpenAPI contract) -> regeneration (reconciles against protected files) -> AI agent implements business logic -> validation by guardrails on every commit (build fails on violations)
Developer defines the domain schema and specification updates (strategic intent); no explicit human review gate described; enforcement is automatic via linters on every commit
Full workflow (Setup with the generator toolchain; Extension with spec update, regeneration, implementation and lint validation)
Spec-as-source (authors' wording: 'positioned firmly within the spec-as-source paradigm but extends it into a continuous governance model'; cites Piskala's levels)
Study 1: new project (bootstrapping a backend from a Prisma schema). Study 2: existing code base (feature extension of the Study 1 baseline repository)
Two Prisma schemas: 14-model event management system and 118-model enterprise platform; extension baseline 1,936 lines; feature: review system across multiple layers
Full-stack/backend REST APIs (event management; enterprise platform)
Not stated (agents run by the author; author's internal use of the toolchain for four months mentioned)
Time per setup session in minutes (Study 1 only, Table I); context tokens only as the DeepSeek-Chat overflow (177K vs 128K limit) on the 118-model schema. No cost metric in Study 2
Coverage of schema entities completed (e.g. 14/14, 18/118, 10/118); 'working feature logic' (functional tests not reported)

Architectural violations (ESLint, Dependency Cruiser); OpenAPI lint score (Spectral); maintainability index (es6-plato, 0-100, Halstead volume, cyclomatic complexity, LOC) and change in MI; maximum cyclomatic complexity; code bloat (extra lines vs governed)
None
Specification drift (endpoints created without updating the OpenAPI contract, qualitative); number of linter correction cycles (qualitative)
Automatic: es6-plato static analysis, ESLint, Dependency Cruiser, Spectral lint; coverage and structural observations by the author (manual inspection)

Agent/harness Not stated for all. Study 1 Setup, 14-model schema: (a) Governed + agent n.s. + DeepSeek-Chat: completed, 5 min, OpenAPI lint 97, 0 violations, MI 78.50. Quality works; cost works. (b) Governed + n.s. + GPT-5-mini: completed, 2 min, lint 97, 0 violations, MI 78.26. Quality: works; cost: works. (c) Governed + n.s. + Kimi K2: completed, 7.9 min, lint 91, 0 violations, MI 77.30. Quality: works; cost: works. (d)-(f) Non-governed + n.s. + DeepSeek-Chat / GPT-5-mini / Kimi K2: all failed coverage and quality (typically 5-8 of 14 entities, no layer separation); per-model values Not stated. Quality: does not work; cost: not measured. Study 1, 118-model schema (governed only): (g) DeepSeek-Chat: failed, context overflow (177K tokens vs 128K limit). Quality: does not work; cost: does not work. (h) Kimi K2: 18/118, 0 violations, same MI. Quality: partly; cost: not measured. (i) GPT-5-mini: 10/118, 0 violations. Quality: partly; cost: not measured. Study 2 Extension (review feature, 1,936-line baseline): (j) Non-governed + Kimi K2: +244 lines vs governed, dMI -1.00, max complexity 13. Quality: partly (works functionally, degraded structure); cost: not measured. (k) Governed + Kimi K2: base lines, dMI +2.10, max CC 4. Quality: works; cost: not measured. (l) Non-governed + DeepSeek-Chat: +834 lines vs governed, dMI -1.99, CC 13. Quality: partly; cost: not measured. (m) Governed + DeepSeek-Chat: dMI +0.90, CC 4, fewest correction cycles. Quality: works; cost: not measured. (n) Non-governed + GPT-5-mini: +186 lines vs governed, dMI -1.43, CC 13. Quality: partly; cost: not measured. (o) Governed + GPT-5-mini: dMI +1.04, CC 4. Quality: works; cost: not measured

Two studies: Setup (bootstrap backend from Prisma schema; 4 repositories: governed/non-governed x small/large schema) and Extension (review system feature from the Study 1 baseline). Configurations: governed vs non-governed x 3 models (DeepSeek-Chat, Kimi K2, GPT-5-mini); large schema governed only. Baseline: non-governed prompt. Held constant: schema/task and model within comparison; prompts differ by condition (governed references toolchain and skills; Extension baseline had tools and linters present but not referenced); agent Not stated. Acceptance tests: none (linters and MI); functional correctness not tested. Repetitions: 1 per configuration (implied). Human intervention: Not stated

Governed better than non-governed for all three models. Setup (14 models): governed all completed with 0 violations and MI 77-78 (<2% variance); non-governed all failed (5-8/14 entities). Extension: non-governed added 186-834 extra lines, MI -1.00 to -1.99, max CC 13; governed MI +0.90 to +2.10 (79.3-79.4), CC 4, 0 violations after linter feedback. Open-weight models comparable to GPT-5-mini under governance. No statistical tests

Distinguished governed from non-governed clearly on structural metrics; did not distinguish models under governance (by design, generators deterministic). Repeatability: single runs, not discussed. Limitations stated: preliminary, only initial development (one feature addition); longitudinal studies needed

Evaluation preliminary, captures only initial development and one feature addition; longitudinal studies over many collaboration cycles needed (only subjective internal use over four months). Large schemas need workflow orchestration for full coverage (context limits). Future work: design-review agents per tool, automated test generation from OpenAPI contracts as guardrails, extension beyond REST to stateful applications

Printed page numbers 194-198 correspond to PDF pages 1-5. Tables I and II layout jumbled by pdftotext; rebuilt row-wise (model order Kimi K2, DeepSeek, GPT-5-mini in Table II; Non-Gov then Gov rows), consistent with text (DeepSeek +834 lines). Text says governed MI 79.3-79.4 in Extension. Setup time measured for the LLM running two commands; author notes developers would run the deterministic flow directly. Agent harness/CLI used to run the models Not stated. Replication package (artifacts, prompts, scripts): https://anonymous.4open.science/r/icsa-replication-07BE/. No pre-registration. Language: JavaScript/TypeScript (Node.js/Express, Prisma ORM, OpenAPI 3.1)

fields.why: The justification counted 'lines' as a cost metric. Lines added (bloat) is internal quality, as the round-2 corrections to Cost metrics and Evaluation already say, and Study 2 reports no cost. The score stays Partly.
